    <title>v1.39.1</title>
    <content type="html"><p><strong>Summary of changes</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Security fixes:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-m745-gh6x-349x">CVE-2026-73511</a>: url normalization: strip path parameters from individual path segments per RFC 3986 section 3.3. Revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.strip_path_parameters_per_segment</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-r6j2-mrm5-72mg">CVE-2026-73512</a>: http3: UAF on a specifically timed sequence of HTTP/3 frames.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-jjmm-fw8p-crpw">CVE-2026-73513</a>: http2: abnormal process termination on trailers received without the END_STREAM flag.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-pv9h-4fxf-7vrg">CVE-2026-73546</a>: admin: sanitize stat names before converting them to HTML. Guarded by <code>envoy.reloadable_features.sanitize_html_stats_names</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-87ph-jqwm-pg6r">CVE-2026-73547</a>: ext_authz: abnormal process termination on requests without a URI path (i.e. CONNECT).</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-3vhp-c83q-jqc2">CVE-2026-73548</a>: http: payload sent before a generic HTTP upgrade was accepted could be interpreted as a pipelined HTTP/1 request and poison a shared upstream connection. Revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.http_pause_generic_upgrade_request_body</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-jp5f-qr64-c9vw">CVE-2026-73549</a>: quic: crash handling scoped IPv6 addresses in QUIC client connections and Original Dst clusters.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-qgf6-qvhw-4hvh">CVE-2026-73550</a>: http2: dropped <code>Host</code> headers now count towards request header map size and count limits. Revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.http2_track_size_of_dropped_host_header</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-2w8w-rfw7-8gg4">CVE-2026-73551</a>: url normalization: strip path parameters from dot and dotdot segments (<code>/.;</code>, <code>/..;</code>) so canonicalization interprets them correctly. Applies only when <code>normalize_path</code> is enabled; revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.strip_dotdot_segments_with_parameters</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-23xh-2qxr-3xv8">CVE-2026-73552</a>: safe_regex: switch charset mode from UTF-8 to Latin1, as HTTP headers are not UTF-8 encoded. Revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.re2_use_latin1_mode</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-77x5-xqjg-hprq">CVE-2026-73553</a>: rbac: RBAC path matching now respects the route's <code>ignore_path_parameters_in_path_matching</code>, preventing authz bypass via appended path parameters. Revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.rbac_respect_ignore_path_parameters</code>.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-q8wp-gf7q-m8cv">CVE-2026-50572</a>: ext_authz: UAF when ext_authz over HTTP causes a request to be rejected.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-5vff-j9p4-38j3">CVE-2026-48521</a>: http3: abnormal process termination when upstream protocol is selected via ALPN and the server uses HTTP/3.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>Bug fixes:</p>
<ul>
<li>http: fixed a filter manager bug where a body frame moved into the filter-manager buffer via <code>addDecodedData()</code>/<code>addEncodedData()</code> immediately before returning <code>Continue</code> was silently dropped, corrupting large streamed bodies. Revert with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.filter_manager_forward_added_data_on_continue</code>.</li>
<li>ext_proc: fixed multiple lifetime bugs in the ext_proc filter and the underlying gRPC async client that could lead to use-after-free or double delivery of callbacks.</li>
<li>tls: fixed a memory leak in the OpenSSL compatibility layer where <code>SSL_get0_peer_certificates()</code> leaked an <code>X509</code> refcount per call, preventing certificates from being freed on connection close.</li>
<li>tls: fixed a bug where OpenSSL used glibc's allocator instead of tcmalloc, operating on a separate heap and making OpenSSL allocations invisible to tcmalloc heap profiling.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

<a href="https://hub.docker.com/r/envoyproxy/envoy/tags?page=1&amp;name=v1.39.1" rel="nofollow">https://hub.docker.com/r/envoyproxy/envoy/tags?page=1&amp;name=v1.39.1</a><br>

<a href="https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.39.1/" rel="nofollow">https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.39.1/</a><br>
<strong>Release notes</strong>:<br>
<a href="https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.39.1/version_history/v1.39/v1.39.1" rel="nofollow">https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.39.1/version_history/v1.39/v1.39.1</a><br>

<a class="commit-link" href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/compare/v1.39.0...v1.39.1"><tt>v1.39.0...v1.39.1</tt></a></p>

Signed-off-by: Ryan Northey <a href="mailto:ryan@synca.io">ryan@synca.io</a></p></content>

    <title>v1.39.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>Summary of changes</h2>
<h2>Breaking changes</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>build</strong>: Envoy now uses Bazel 8. Because Envoy still uses WORKSPACE mode, <code>--enable_workspace</code> and <code>--noenable_bzlmod</code> are required and have been added to <code>.bazelrc</code>; external-repository runfiles now appear directly under the runfiles root.</li>
<li><strong>build</strong>: the Intel DLB connection balancer (<code>envoy.network.connection_balance.dlb</code>) is disabled for all builds due to a broken source archive.</li>
<li><strong>TLS</strong>: <code>enforce_rsa_key_usage</code> is deprecated and ignored; Envoy now always enforces the certificate <code>keyUsage</code> extension.</li>
<li><strong>TLS inspector</strong>: client TLS versions are validated and must be between TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.3 (revertible via <code>envoy.reloadable_features.tls_inspector_enforce_client_tls_version</code>).</li>
<li><strong>OpenTelemetry tracing</strong>: the tracer now honors Envoy's request-entry sampling decision, including <code>overall_sampling</code>, even when propagated trace context or the configured sampler requests sampling. This may reduce exported spans.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Security</h3>
<ul>
<li>HTTP/2 now counts uncompressed cookies toward header-size and header-count limits (<strong>CVE-2026-47774</strong>), strengthens PRIORITY/WINDOW_UPDATE flood protection, and adds configurable nghttp2 RST_STREAM rate limits.</li>
<li>HTTP/3 fixes cover QPACK blocked-decoding denial of service (<strong><a title="GHSA-p7c7-7c47-pwch" href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-p7c7-7c47-pwch">GHSA-p7c7-7c47-pwch</a></strong>) and inconsistent headers-only <code>content-length</code> handling (<strong>CVE-2026-48743</strong>).</li>
<li>Security fixes were added for ext_authz (<strong>CVE-2026-47205</strong>), ext_proc (<strong>CVE-2026-47207</strong>), gRPC stats (<strong>CVE-2026-47204</strong>), internal redirects (<strong>CVE-2026-47221</strong>), and OAuth2 lifecycle handling (<strong>CVE-2026-48090</strong>).</li>
<li>OAuth2 adds AES-256-GCM cookie encryption to address <strong>CVE-2026-47775</strong>. Migration is opt-in: enable <code>oauth2_use_gcm_encryption</code>, monitor <code>oauth_legacy_cbc_decrypt</code>, then disable <code>oauth2_legacy_cbc_decrypt_compat</code>.</li>
<li>Additional fixes cover DNS query validation (<strong>CVE-2026-48497</strong>), JSON nesting limits (<strong>CVE-2026-48042</strong>), PROXY protocol TLV smuggling (<strong>CVE-2026-47692</strong>), formatter crashes (<strong>CVE-2026-47220</strong>), TCP StatsD overflow (<strong>CVE-2026-48706</strong>), TLS SAN NUL handling (<strong>CVE-2026-47778</strong>), and Zstd decompression memory exhaustion (<strong>CVE-2026-48044</strong>).</li>
<li>New upstream RBAC and dynamic-forward-proxy resolved-address filtering provide CIDR-based protection against SSRF after DNS resolution and host selection.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Dynamic modules</h3>
<ul>
<li>New extension points: access-log/header formatters, downstream and upstream transport sockets, active health checkers, and stats sinks.</li>
<li>Cluster load balancers can read host stats, read and write dynamic metadata and filter state, and publish main-thread state to worker-local slots.</li>
<li>Modules can emit metrics from configuration and background contexts; loading and initialization failures now expose server-wide counters tagged by extension instance.</li>
<li>Added validation-mode detection, network/listener attribute access, batched header and metadata APIs, effective log-level access, and zero-copy borrowed buffers in the Rust SDK.</li>
<li>Fixed listener HTTP-callout crashes, watermark initialization, streaming-response re-entry, independent decode/encode continuation, CatchUnwind re-entry, <code>Struct</code> configuration handling, and HTTP/TCP bridge buffer overflow with more than 64 slices.</li>
</ul>
<h3>MCP (Model Context Protocol) and AI protocols</h3>
<ul>
<li>Added a Wuffs-backed streaming JSON parser for MCP, A2A, OpenAI, Anthropic, and related protocols, with bounded field capture, incremental parsing, no DOM allocation, and duplicate-key detection.</li>
<li>MCP filtering now exposes processing status, supports configurable duplicate-key rejection, and improves oversized-body behavior for pass-through and rejection modes.</li>
<li>MCP router adds elicitation and server-to-client request routing, plus lazy per-backend initialization.</li>
<li>MCP JSON REST Bridge adds per-route tool configuration and locally generated <code>tools/list</code> responses.</li>
</ul>
<h3>HTTP, routing and protocol</h3>
<ul>
<li>New HTTP filters provide weighted bandwidth sharing and selectable sub-filter chains with per-route configuration.</li>
<li><code>HeaderMatcher</code> now evaluates separately supplied header values individually instead of matching only their comma-joined representation (revertible via <code>envoy.reloadable_features.match_headers_individually</code>).</li>
<li>HTTP inspector uses Balsa by default and now fast-fails invalid non-HTTP method bytes instead of buffering up to 64 KiB.</li>
<li>Added drain-timeout and maximum-connection-duration jitter to reduce synchronized reconnect spikes.</li>
<li>Routing gains cluster refresh on retries, weighted-cluster reselection, formatter/CEL-based redirect paths, and mixed literal/variable URI-template segments.</li>
<li>Fixed connection-pool re-entrancy, connectivity-grid teardown and duplicate-attempt bugs, stale on-demand cluster information, and handling of HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 <code>RST_STREAM(NO_ERROR)</code> after complete responses.</li>
</ul>
<h3>TLS, authentication and authorization</h3>
<ul>
<li>Added CNSA 1.0/2.0 compliance policies, TLS group formatters for identifying post-quantum key exchange, and suppression of oversized client CA lists.</li>
<li>QUIC supports opt-in TLS key logging and session-ticket resumption.</li>
<li>TLS certificate compression via the brotli runtime guard is disabled by default; TLS sockets also gain improved connection-reset reporting.</li>
<li>OAuth2 adds <code>PRIVATE_KEY_JWT</code>, ID-token forwarding, configurable post-logout redirects, access-token-based cookie lifetime, and safe original-request URI formatting with redirect-domain allowlists.</li>
<li>BasicAuth supports missing-credential pass-through and authenticated-username metadata; JWT extraction can mark forwarded claims whose signatures were not verified.</li>
</ul>
<h3>DNS, load balancing and upstream</h3>
<ul>
<li>The unified DNS cluster implementation is enabled by default; equivalent c-ares resolvers can be shared across clusters to support shared qcache.</li>
<li>DNS clusters gain a minimum TTL refresh floor, while dynamic forward proxy sub-clusters can use <code>DnsCluster</code> configuration and resolved-address CIDR filtering.</li>
<li>Client-side weighted round robin adds out-of-band ORCA reporting with configurable port, authority, and transport socket matching.</li>
<li>Least-request load balancing can optionally account for pending requests, with a new per-endpoint pending-request gauge.</li>
<li>Fixed EDS hostname updates, load reports containing only custom metrics or completed requests, and dynamic-forward-proxy lookup teardown.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Networking and system performance</h3>
<ul>
<li>Linux deployments gain worker CPU affinity and an <code>SO_REUSEPORT</code> BPF connection balancer for CPU-local connection steering.</li>
<li>Added a Linux sockmap socket interface for accelerating same-host TCP traffic through eBPF.</li>
<li>io_uring adds multishot receives, adaptive read buffers, and configurable write backpressure.</li>
<li>Reverse tunnels gain opt-in GOAWAY-aware draining and replacement; MySQL proxy adds downstream TLS termination with <code>caching_sha2_password</code> mediation.</li>
<li>Added UDP proxy external authorization, network ext_proc metadata reception, and early external-processor stream closure.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Observability</h3>
<ul>
<li>New access-log data includes upstream TLS SNI and HTTP/TCP downstream/upstream connection duration points; gRPC access logging adds delivery success/failure counters.</li>
<li>Added dynamic-module and Wasm programmable stats sinks, OpenTelemetry metric request chunking, endpoint observability names, and default-tag overrides.</li>
<li>Prometheus scraping and large-scale stat-reference release are substantially faster; <code>/peak_heap_dump</code> exposes tcmalloc's peak heap profile.</li>
<li>Added process-wide Lua and Wasm VM gauges, single-entry stack traces, and an Envoy-version log-format token.</li>
<li>Tap now honors configured runtime sampling and reports sampled-out requests/connections.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Rate limiting and configuration</h3>
<ul>
<li>Rate limiting adds static and dynamic per-descriptor limit overrides, zero-token always-reject behavior, and configurable response-metadata namespaces.</li>
<li>GCP authentication supports bound access tokens, bound JWTs, and unbound access tokens from the metadata server.</li>
<li>Added file-backed IP tagging, in-place watched-file modification events, runtime-adjustable fixed-heap limits, health-check HTTP status events, and xDS unsubscribe callbacks.</li>
<li>Redis proxy adds Redis 7.4 hash-field expiry commands and permits custom commands inside transactions.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Other notable changes and fixes</h3>
<ul>
<li>Fixed Hickory DNS resolver leaks and use-after-free, file-server cancellation use-after-free, Golang filter re-entry, outlier-detection teardown, missing network namespaces, and asynchronous TLS close handling.</li>
<li>Fixed RTDS guard removal, VHDS subscriptions, Wasm VM cache invalidation when environment variables change, and upstream Wasm metric scoping.</li>
<li>Improved UDP proxy attempted-host and address logging, Zipkin timestamp trace IDs, gRPC access-log failure accounting, and health-check event detail.</li>
<li>Added TCP proxy delayed route selection, drain-close handling, and connection-duration access logging.</li>
</ul>

<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-7q3f-gwg7-j8g4">CVE-2026-48706</a>: Envoy Heap Buffer Overflow in TcpStatsdSink</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/security/advisories/GHSA-p7c7-7c47-pwch">GHSA-p7c7-7c47-pwch</a>:  Denial-of-Service Attack Against the HTTP/3 Stack via QPACK Blocked Decoding</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>Upstream security fixes:</p>
<ul>
<li><a title="CVE-2026-47261" data-hovercard-type="advisory" data-hovercard-url="/advisories/GHSA-2r75-cxrj-cmph/hovercard" href="https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2r75-cxrj-cmph">CVE-2026-47261</a>: wasm: bumped <code>com_github_wasmtime</code> to resolve <a title="CVE-2026-47261" data-hovercard-type="advisory" data-hovercard-url="/advisories/GHSA-2r75-cxrj-cmph/hovercard" href="https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2r75-cxrj-cmph">CVE-2026-47261</a>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>

<ul>
<li>build: disabled the contrib extension <code>envoy.network.connection_balance.dlb</code> (Intel DLB connection balancer) at the Bazel layer for all builds and platforms due to a breakage at the source archive.     <content type="html"><p><strong>Summary of changes</strong>:</p>

    <title>v1.38.2</title>
    <content type="html"><p><strong>Summary of changes</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Bug fixes:</p>
<ul>
<li>runtime: fixed RTDS runtime guard override removal so deleting an override restores the process-wide runtime guard value to the default value.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>New features:</p>
<ul>
<li>http2: added opt-in histograms for HTTP/2 header statistics, including header-entry count, header-map byte size, reassembled <code>cookie</code> header length, and individual <code>cookie</code> header count. Enable with <code>envoy.reloadable_features.http2_record_histograms</code>; the histograms and runtime guard will be removed in a future Envoy release.</li>
<li>http2: added <code>envoy.reloadable_features.http2_max_cookies_size_in_kb</code> to limit the size of the reassembled <code>cookie</code> header. By default, no cookie-size limit is enforced.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
